newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.S. planning another attack on Iraq, Baghdad says.
newsitem.headline: U.S. planning another attack on Iraq, Baghdad says.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said on Tuesday the United States was beefing up its military presence in the Gulf to launch another military strike against his country.

"American pretexts and excuses for the massing of troops and weapons in the Arab Gulf region are aimed at the staging of an aggression on Iraq," Aziz said in a statement carried by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA).

INA said Aziz was reacting to statements by U.S. officials that Washington was determined to do everything possible to secure the safety of its pilots patrolling no-fly zones for Iraqi aircraft in Iraq's south and north.
"The preparation for the staging of one aggression after another comes when the Americans find that circumstances are suitable and serve their policies and election interests," Aziz said.

The confrontation between Iraq and the United States began late last month when Baghdad's forces intervened to help a Kurdish faction in northern Iraq -- an area closed to them since the end of the Gulf war in 1991.

U.S. President Bill Clinton, facing a presidential election in less than two months, was attacked on Tuesday by opposition Republicans for the lack of impact from two U.S. cruise missile attacks on Iraq he ordered in reprisal.
INA also said Aziz had sent a letter to U.N. Secretary- General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
In it he described flights by U.S. and allied warplanes over Iraq as "a military action constituting a flagrant aggression of Iraq's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence."
INA carried another letter from Aziz to Ghali protesting against "the frequent Iranian provocative and aggressive military operations along Iraqi borders."

Iraqi troops backed Kurdistan Democratic Party forces in the capture of the northern Kurdish city of Arbil this month from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), which Baghdad says is Iranian-backed.
Regarding the massing of U.S. troops in the Gulf, Aziz said it was clear that Washington's "pretexts and allegations...had no legal basis and lacked sound logic."

"Now they speak about the safety of their pilots who violate the airspace of a sovereign country in contravention of international law and U.N. resolutions...and they issue more and more statements as if their planes are flying over California's airspace," he said.
